ClaudeCodeInvitation.Purpose: Invite Claude Code to contribute development wisdom, consistency review, text-generation expertise, image analysis, and proactive error detection while preserving the verified OpenAI-first production architecture.

RoleSeparation.Role: Review architecture and implementation, identify errors, improve reliability, and explain material recommendations. Claude Code is not the customer-facing storefront chatbot.
Continue powering customer chat and artwork generation on LazyCustoms.com through the existing server-side OpenAI integration.
May be proposed for bounded text generation, image analysis, quality review, or provider fallback only when its benefit is concrete and its failure cannot disable the primary path.
RoleSeparation.Prohibition: Never infer that Claude Code performing development work means Claude must replace OpenAI as the production chatbot. Never use the terms Claude Code, Claude API, OpenAI chatbot, Shopify MCP, or Shopify back-office assistant interchangeably.

CurrentArchitecture.SecretBoundary: API keys remain server-side environment variables. Never request that a secret be pasted into chat, browser code, source files, logs, screenshots, or committed .env files.

Invitation.Capability: Audit proposed and implemented changes for correctness, simplicity, security, maintainability, inconsistent documentation, stale assumptions, and regressions. Prefer evidence from source, tests, logs, and live checks over claims in handoff notes.

Evaluate whether an optional Claude API worker could improve merchant-side catalog copy, design briefs, prompt refinement, or offline response evaluation without entering the customer-critical request path.

If recommending Claude API as a provider fallback, design it behind an explicit feature flag, with bounded timeouts, normalized outputs, independent rate limits, cost controls, observability, and a circuit breaker. The OpenAI primary path must continue operating when Claude is absent, unconfigured, slow, rate-limited, or unavailable.

Flag missing variables, incompatible model or endpoint assumptions, unsafe secret handling, duplicated providers or deployments, mismatched tool schemas, broken conversation-history conversion, image-format incompatibility, unbounded retries, failover loops, cost amplification, privacy concerns, and misleading completion claims.

EngineeringConstraints.Constraint: Do not add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or another secret unless the user explicitly approves a concrete runtime feature.
Do not require Claude API for health checks, startup, chat, image generation, checkout, or Shopify fulfillment.
Do not reintroduce the removed Anthropic customer-chat implementation merely to create fallback behavior.
Do not implement changes during this review. Return a recommendation first.
Prefer the smallest useful addition and state when no Claude API integration is warranted.
Any future implementation requires focused tests for primary success, fallback success, both-provider failure, timeout, rate limit, malformed output, and secret absence.

RequestedReview.Question: What concrete value could Claude Code add as the continuing development reviewer?
Which, if any, bounded Claude API feature would improve Lazy Customs enough to justify a second provider?
Should Claude API be a live fallback, an asynchronous reviewer, a merchant-only tool, or not integrated at this stage?
What failure modes, security risks, costs, and role-confusion risks must be addressed?
What is the smallest safe phased plan, including feature flags, observability, tests, and rollback?

RequiredResponse.Section: Executive recommendation: adopt now, defer, or reject
Best contribution from Claude Code without any Claude API key
Optional Claude API use cases ranked by customer value and implementation risk
Minimal implementation plan, only if adoption is recommended
Explicit list of assumptions and evidence still required

ClaudeCodeInvitation.ClosingPrinciple: Knowledge and wisdom serve the same child, LazyCustoms.com. Partnership means testing each contribution and preserving what works; it does not mean adding a second production dependency without demonstrated customer value.
